newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- About 33,000 Moslem and Christian residents of remote villages have poured into Pikit town, North Cotabato as of Tuesday as the military pounded anew Moslem rebel positions, Mayor Motin Molingco said on Wednesday. Fourteen more rebels were killed yesterday as the military mounted attacks. (MALAYA/INQUIRER)
- The Armed Forces chief rebuked Naval sailors who on Sunday fired warning shots to drive away Chinese fishing vessels near two islands being claimed by the Philippines in the Spratlys. (INQUIRER)

- The Senate ways and means committee, wrapping up its deliberations on the controversial Comprehensive Tax Reform Programme, yesterday reduced the House-approved tax-exempt salary for a family of 146,000 pesos to 98,000 pesos. (BULLETIN)

- The country's current account deficit widened by 22 percent to $1.13 billion in the first quarter of 1997 from $923 million in the same period in 1996, the Central Bank reported yesterday. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The government fumbled in its bid yesterday to privatise Food Terminal Inc due to several restrictions on the development of the 120-hectare property. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Board of Investments rejected yesterday the proposal of mining firms for special incentives. (BULLETIN/MALAYA)
